sources.title: J. S. Grewal, The Sikh Empire (1799-1849), Cambridge University Press
sources.note: Authoritative synthesis of Ranjit Singh unification, government, army, revenue, trade, religious diversity and the state later history.

sources.title: The Punjab under Maharaja Ranjit Singh, Australian National University Open Research
sources.note: Scholarly political chronology used for Kasur and the early consolidation sequence without relying on the atlas polygon.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Misls
sources.note: Punjabi University reference on the eighteenth-century Sikh misls, Lahore, Ranjit Singh entry in 1799 and regional trade.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Khalsa
sources.note: Punjabi University reference distinguishing the initiated Khalsa collective and its 1699 origin from a later territorial state.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Afghan-Sikh Relations
sources.note: Chronology of Lahore, Attock, failed Multan campaigns through 1815 and later conquests of Multan, Kashmir and Peshawar.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Anglo-Sikh Treaty of Amritsar (1809)
sources.note: Date, terms and political consequences of the 1809 treaty separating Cis-Sutlej ambitions from northern consolidation.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Lahore Darbar
sources.note: Punjabi University account of the State of Lahore, Sarkar Khalsaji, personalized rule and multi-faith officeholding.

sources.title: Symbols, Community and Contest in the Politics of Sikh Identity, Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of cross-faith appointments, Muslim elites, shrine grants and state-building through religious patronage.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Army of Maharaja Ranjit Singh
sources.note: Early infantry training, varied recruitment, gun manufacture, artillery and the chronology of later European officers.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Khalsa Darbar Records
sources.note: Surviving Persian official records from 1811, including early troop accounts, revenue categories and administrative documentation.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Sikh Coins
sources.note: Chronology and interpretation of Lahore and Amritsar Nanakshahi coinage under Ranjit Singh.

sources.title: Paramdip Kaur Khera, Catalogue of Sikh Coins in the British Museum
sources.note: British Museum Research Publication 190 with catalogued legends, transliteration, translation, dates, weights and mints.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Jagirdari
sources.note: Land-revenue assignments, collection in cash or kind, service obligations and limits of jagir tenure under Sikh rule.

sources.title: British Punjab and the Dialectics of Primitive Accumulation, International Review of Social History
sources.note: Peer-reviewed account of Punjab agrarian relations, jagirdari, products, pastoral tribute and later colonial transformation.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Gurmukhi
sources.note: History of the Gurmukhi script in scripture, community schooling and its administrative spread under Ranjit Singh.

sources.title: Empires, Languages, and Scripts in the Perso-Indian World, Comparative Studies in Society and History
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of multilingual Punjab education, institutional grants, Persian, Gurmukhi and commercial Landa schooling.

sources.title: Robina Shoeb, Refocusing on Education System under Sikh Rule, University of the Punjab
sources.note: Historical study of schools, home tutors, religious institutions, curricula and gender, used with retrospective evidence cautions.

sources.title: Priya Atwal, Royals and Rebels: The Rise and Fall of the Sikh Empire, Oxford University Press
sources.note: Scholarly reconstruction of the ruling family, queens, princes, dynastic politics and gendered power beyond one-man biography.

sources.title: Radha Kapuria, Of Music and the Maharaja, Modern Asian Studies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Lahore court music, female performers, gender, affect and power across Ranjit Singh reign.

sources.title: Life at Lahore Darbar 1799-1839, University of the Punjab
sources.note: Court-specific study of palaces, ceremony, alms, music and sacred bathing, kept separate from ordinary household life.

sources.title: Lahore: A Study in Space and Time, Pakistan Geographical Review
sources.note: University study of Lahore urban form, walls, rebuilding, settlement and later growth under Ranjit Singh.

sources.title: The Lahore Darbar: the Court of Lahore, Wallace Collection
sources.note: Museum essay on court exchange, gifts, textiles, metalwork, trade, havelis and the golden throne.

sources.title: Ranjit Singh Army and His Firangis, Wallace Collection
sources.note: Museum chronology placing Allard, Ventura and the Fauj-i-Khas after 1822, outside the target map interval.

sources.title: Maharaja Ranjit Singh in a Bazaar, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Museum record for a circa 1830 to 1840 Lahore painting and its reuse of stock figures rather than documentary street reportage.

sources.title: British Library Add Or 1397-1451, Trades and Occupations in Lahore
sources.note: Catalogue of 55 circa 1860 Lahore drawings showing occupations, wells, irrigation, laundry, foods, toys and family groupings after annexation.

sources.title: The Golden Temple at Amritsar, National Army Museum
sources.note: Museum record identifying major marble and gold decoration during Ranjit Singh reign while preserving the shrine longer history.

sources.title: First Sikh War, National Army Museum
sources.note: Museum military history of the kingdom after Ranjit Singh, army strength, regency conflict and the 1845 to 1846 war.

sources.title: Second Sikh War, National Army Museum
sources.note: Museum military history of the 1848 to 1849 war and formal British annexation of Punjab on 29 March 1849.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Doctor John Martin Honigberger
sources.note: Later court physician evidence for overlapping allopathic, homeopathic, Ayurvedic and Unani practice after 1829.

sources.title: History of Lahore, Government of the Punjab
sources.note: Official city chronology placing a sanitation committee in 1858 and piped municipal waterworks in 1882, both later than the target.

sources.title: Colonialism and Sanitary Medicine in Punjab, Modern Asian Studies
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology of formal preventive-health policy after 1860, useful for preventing back-projection into Sikh rule.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Bhangian di Top
sources.note: History of the Zamzama cannon, its capture at Amritsar and campaign use without turning one gun into the whole army.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, Bhandari Papers
sources.note: Description of thousands of Persian letters and legal, revenue, mortgage, grant and court documents from Sikh-period Punjab.

proposedOverrides.summary: Ranjit Singh's early State of Lahore in the atlas 1800 to 1815 display window.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id sikhs is preserved, but the card corrects its subject from a whole faith and people to Ranjit Singh early State of Lahore or Sikh Empire.
The exact interval is one approximate atlas display from 1800 to 1815. It is not the founding and fall of Sikhism, Sikh communities or the historical empire.
No appliesTo alias is added. Lahore, Afghanistan, Multan, Maratha, British and neighboring state records remain distinct.
The sole geometry is one 35-position Polygon with SHA-256 2cd9186c13755098f800c6d299b2c5001c9b57b4a8eab40d00cd2f2820f187b5.
The polygon wrongly includes Multan, Kashmir, Peshawar and Cis-Sutlej states while excluding Anandpur Sahib, so it is preserved only as audited display geometry.
The 1815 Maratha replacement is a data error. The override records fell null, the card ending status is continuity, and no successor is inferred.
The authentic writing sample is a normalized Persian clause from an 1801 Lahore Nanakshahi rupee, with transliteration, translation and facsimile limits.
Ordinary family, education, medicine, food, clothing, housing, water, play and sanitation evidence is distinguished from court sources and later comparative material.
